survivingClaim: Precise obstruction, no statement about zeta zeros. The Ramaré/Matomäki-Radziwiłł factorisation supplies no every-window or one-sided statement. (i) Bandwidth alpha in (1,2) in the inertia chain is the averaged Hardy-Littlewood bound |(1/H) sum_{h<=H}(1-h/H)E(h)| << X^(1/alpha) log X with H = X^(1-1/alpha): a power saving of exponent 1-1/alpha over the sieve bound, against proved log-power savings (recalled from memory, H >= X^(8/33)); on V(X,H) this bound would exclude isolated zeros with beta > 1/2+1/(2 alpha). (ii) Outputs are mean squares on Re s = 1; the large-value count at threshold P^-a is (TP)^(2a+o(1)), T^(2a) when P^k = T, against exponent 0 needed to exclude a zero at a = 1-sigma. (iii) Pretentious and log-averaged statements are unconditional theorems, invariant under finite modification and rotation, with tolerances (log x)^-A above the size x^(beta-1) of a zero term. DH (trivially, periodic coefficients), Liouville, bounded twists and unimodular twists satisfy the method's conclusions. Lemma D verified numerically for zeta to 7e-11; the DH peak is consistent in size only, not separated from background.
obstruction: (i) Bandwidth alpha in (1,2) in the inertia chain needs the Fejer-averaged Hardy-Littlewood error below X^(1/alpha) log X with H = X^(1-1/alpha): a power saving of exponent 1-1/alpha, against proved log-power savings (range H >= X^(8/33) recalled, source not opened). (ii) Outputs are mean squares on Re s = 1; the large-value count at threshold P^-a is T^(2a), against exponent 0 needed at a = 1-sigma to exclude a zero. (iii) Pretentious and log-averaged statements are invariant under finite modification and rotation (tail type), with tolerances (log x)^-A above the size x^(beta-1) of a zero term. The method's conclusions are closed under linear combination, so DH satisfies them: multiplicativity is essential to the proof, not to the conclusion class. MV-CAP and tail type.

lesson: The Matomäki-Radziwiłł family is a mean-value device on Re s = 1 whose saving is capped at a power of log (integers without a prime factor in [P,Q] have density about log P/log Q). Its conclusions are closed under linear combination, so DH passes: multiplicativity is essential to the proof, not to the conclusion class. A zero at beta < 1 enters at relative size x^(beta-1), below every tolerance in the family. Add it to the closed families under MV-CAP and tail type.

It is a density statement and was not compared with the density literature.
